texts.preamble: Kanai Paria & Anr vs The State Of West Bengal on 18 December, 2017 Author: Debi Prosad Dey Bench: Debi Prosad Dey 1 18.12.2017 In The High Court At Calcutta Sl.14 (Criminal Revisional Jurisdiction) Ct-35 Appellate Side (Ad) C.R.R. No.2020 of 2016 In the matter of: Kanai Paria & Anr. vs. The State of West Bengal Mr. Abhijit Kumar ADhya. Adv. ... for the State.
texts.arguments: Learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners contends that the report of the expert does not reveal that obnoxious materials were used in the alleged adulteration of the mustard oil and accordingly, the offence ought to be tried by learned Magistrate in stead of by learned Sessions Judge. In support of his contention, learned Advocate for the petitioners has referred to the aforesaid decision as well as a decision reported in AIR 1983 SC 150. Ms. Anusua Sinha, learned Advocate appearing for the State, submits that the factual aspect of the case under reference cannot be looked into in a revisional application and that Section 272 along with the State amendment has not yet been declared unconstitutional by the Hon'ble Apex Court. Ms. Sinha further submits that the case ought to be tried by learned Sessions Judge and there is absolutely no illegality in the order passed by learned Additional Sessions Judge, Fast Track Court-III, Howrah. Kanai Paria & Anr vs The State Of West Bengal on 18 December, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18397961/ 1 The decision reported in AIR 1983 SC 150 reveals that the Hon'ble Apex Court has considered lesser punishment of the appellant in view of Section 16(1)(a) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954.
